mechanism: Ginkgo biloba may inhibit CYP3A4 and CYP2C9, potentially increasing ethosuximide levels, though ethosuximide is primarily metabolized via glucuronidation with minor CYP involvement.
action: Monitor for signs of ethosuximide toxicity (dizziness, nausea, ataxia); consider serum level monitoring if high-dose ginkgo is used concurrently with ethosuximide.
